title: 2026-11-05 Redwood migration demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jamal (NovaHealth CTO), Hannah (ML Eng), Marco (Head of Security), Leah (PM)

Auto-summary: Quick demo and parity mapping conversation, console and optimize overview, security Qs, agree POC.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jamal: Good, thanks Alex, excited to see how Redwood maps to our current OpenAI + Anthropic setup.
[00:12] Priya: Great, i'll do the technical walk through after a quick overview. we'll focus on API parity, console rollout and Optimize suggestions for your workload.
[00:20] Leah: Quick ask — we care most about latency for clinical workflows and data residency, also cost is a big factor.
[00:28] Alex: Perfect, noted. Marco, you'll probably have security questions — feel free to jump in anytime.
[00:33] Marco: sure, i'll ask about KMS, SSO, and audit logs when we get to it.
[00:38] Priya: Alright i'm going to share my screen — starting with the Redwood API mapping. so OpenAI-style calls map pretty directly, e.g. generation endpoints, you can pass max_tokens, temperature, top_p, and we support streaming. there are small differences in parameter names sometimes, we have a mapping doc we'll share.
[00:55] Hannah: Are function calls supported? we use them heavily for structured outputs.
[00:58] Priya: yes, we support function/tool calling semantics. sometimes the exact signature is slightly different — for example, the content-type and how we encode tool schemas, but we expose SDK helpers to translate from OpenAI shape to Redwood shape. we'll include examples for Anthropic too.
[01:15] Jamal: what about model variants? we currently use a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic models depending on task.
[01:21] Priya: Redwood has a model catalog with curated open models and redwood-verified profiles. you can route by model name, or use smart routing by policy — e.g., latency-first goes to low-latency variant, cost-first to a quantized variant.
[01:35] Alex: on the demo i'll show the console routes and the optimize suggestions that recommend quantization or batching based on observed seq lengths.
[01:45] Priya: jumping into the console — here is the per-route dashboard, token cost breakdowns, and tracing. you can see historical latency P50/P95 and token counts.
[01:58] Leah: that token cost view looks helpful, can we map it back to feature flags / product routes?
[02:02] Priya: yes, routes map to API keys and to logical product routes. you can tag and filter.
[02:08] Marco: quick security interjection — where are logs stored? and does customer data touch the control plane?
[02:14] Alex: good question — for hosted we retain minimal logs by default, you can opt for Private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed. we also offer KMS integration and HSM for key material; we'll send SOC2/ISO docs.
[02:26] Marco: Do you support SSO / SAML? we need enterprise SSO and RBAC.
[02:30] Priya: yes, SSO (SAML/OIDC) and fine-grained RBAC are supported. audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private customers.
[02:38] Hannah: on the API latency — can you run a quick latency example from hosted vs dedicated?
[02:43] Priya: sure — i'll run a short curl against the hosted endpoint, then we'll show Dedicated numbers from our internal dashboard.
[02:49] [demo noises]
[03:05] Priya: Hosted 1-shot gen, 256 tokens: 120ms p50, 420ms p95 in this region. Dedicated with pinned GPU for the same model: 80ms p50, 210ms p95 in our internal test. your numbers will vary based on prompt patterns and seq lengths.
[03:24] Jamal: that p95 improvement is promising. how much more expensive is Dedicated?
[03:29] Alex: Dedicated is committed capacity pricing — often better unit economics at scale depending on your traffic profile. we'll include a cost estimate in the pricing sheet.
[03:36] Leah: can Redwood Optimize suggest batch sizes and quantization profiles automatically?
[03:40] Priya: yes, Optimize looks at your trace and suggests batching window, KV cache settings, and quantization levels per-model. it can recommend switching to an 8-bit quantized profile for non-critical outputs and keep critical routes on FP16.
[03:52] Hannah: we have some sensitive PHI-like data in prompts. can you guarantee it won't be used to train models?
[03:58] Alex: Redwood does not use customer data to train public models. for Hosted we offer data isolation and opt-out controls, and for Private deployments your data never leaves your VPC. we will send the data handling policy and add it to the SOC docs.
[04:10] Marco: what about encryption at rest and in transit? and KMS?
[04:14] Priya: encryption TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest, with optional customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM modules available for Dedicated/Private.
[04:24] Jamal: good. about differences migrating Anthropic calls — any gotchas?
[04:29] Priya: Anthropic-style safety parameters are supported but names differ; we provide a mapping table and tests. also note that output formatting and temperature semantics can vary between models, so part of the POC is to run evals on your prompt sets to ensure parity.
[04:45] Leah: do you do automatic fallback if a model is unavailable?
[04:48] Alex: yes, policy-based fallback to compatible variants or other regions. automatic fallback is configurable per-route.
[04:54] Hannah: for embeddings, do you support batching and semantic search indexes?
[04:56] Priya: embeddings endpoint supports batch calls and streaming for big jobs; we have integrations for vector stores and recommend precomputing with Optimize suggestions.
[05:05] [15 minute mark, progressed through demo screens showing mapping doc link]
[05:10] Priya: i'm opening the parity mapping doc — we'll share this after the call. it shows OpenAI param -> Redwood param, Anthropic param mappings and code snippets for python/curl/js SDKs.
[05:23] Jamal: sample? can you show a code snippet converting an openai chat call to Redwood?
[05:27] Priya: sure, here's a quick snippet — (reads) 'client.responses.create' maps to 'redwood.responses.generate' and the 'messages' field stays mostly the same, function schemas need a slight wrapper. we'll paste these exact snippets.
[05:42] Leah: what about rate limits? we have bursty daytime traffic.
[05:46] Alex: rate limits configurable per-tenant; Dedicated gives headroom and autoscaling/burst options. you can also set per-route quotas.
[05:53] Marco: for compliance we need a list of sub-processors and a contract addendum for data processing.
[05:58] Alex: we'll attach our DPA and list of sub-processors; Priya will flag the legal pack.
[06:03] Hannah: for the POC, what's the suggested test plan?
[06:06] Priya: we recommend 2-week POC: week 1 run parity functional tests and correctness evals on 3 prompt sets, week 2 run load and latency benchmarks with your traffic profile on dedicated trial. we'll collect metrics and produce a report comparing cost per token and p95 latency.
[06:19] Jamal: timeline looks good. can you support approx 1M tokens/day during POC?
[06:23] Priya: yes, we can provision a trial pool; we'll size it based on your traffic profile once you share sample traffic stats.
[06:30] [07:00] Alex: quick note on billing — hosted is usage billed, Dedicated is reserved with monthly commit. we'll provide sample cost scenarios.
[07:08] Leah: for the retrofit, will we need to change many SDK calls? we have a lot of product routes.
[07:11] Priya: minimal changes ideally; we provide shims and an SDK compatibility layer. most customers map endpoints and use the same message payloads, with a few helper conversions.
[07:20] Marco: any penetration test results we can review?
[07:23] Alex: yes, we'll include pen-test summary and compliance documents in the pack.
[07:29] Hannah: on the Optimize recommendations — can those be automated or just suggestions?
[07:33] Priya: they can be suggestions initially; some automations are available (e.g., auto batching thresholds) but full automations require you enable them. we can run them in read-only mode for the POC so you can review before applying.
[07:46] Leah: what about region routing? we need EU residency for some routes.
[07:50] Alex: routing by region is supported; you can pin routes to EU-only models and data residency. Private deployment is the strongest option for strict residency.
[07:59] Jamal: ok let's go over the immediate deliverables.
[08:02] Alex: action items: i'll send parity mapping doc and pricing, Priya will spin up trial dedicated instance, NovaHealth to share prompts and traffic. we'll schedule kickoff next week.
[08:10] Marco: one more on audit logs retention — default retention is 30 days? we may need longer.
[08:15] Priya: default hosted retention is 30 days, Dedicated/Private support customizable retention windows — we'll include options and cost.
[08:22] Leah: thanks, this was helpful. any final questions?
[08:25] Jamal: none from me, excited to start the POC.
[08:28] Alex: great, closing notes — expect docs from us by Monday and i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the POC kickoff. thanks everyone.
[08:35] [call ends]

References shared: parity-mapping.xlsx (link), pricing-sheet.pdf (link), SOC2-pack.zip (link), sample-sdk-snippets.md (link)

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions of model names (e.g., Redwood Dedicatede), filler words preserved, speaker labels are actual attendee names when possible.
